design:
D1 Tier 2. Hazards: the one-shot worker, which has run with no tools, gains Read for this job; and one route is exempt from the global 1 MB body cap. No migration: files live under knowledge/sources/ beside their metadata, and the distillation firing records the reading. Rollback is a revert; a file source left behind lists on the previous Hub as a source with no text (read_entry already answers None content). The bundle reaches :8000's app on its next reload; until its Hub restarts the file route answers 404 and the page shows the transcription alone.

D2 Read natively, measured (F573). 2026-10-12, claude 2.1.291, claude-haiku-4-5, cwd a directory holding the files: `--tools Read` returned a two-page reportlab PDF's three lines and a PIL PNG's two lines character for character ($0.039 and $0.018); `--tools ""` could not. Codex and Copilot were not measured (Codex undrivable; drives bind Haiku), so they answer cannot-read. Rejected: an extractor (pypdf is not a Hub dependency and images would need OCR, a native dependency).

D3 Transcribe, then distil. The worker writes down the file's text once; it is stored as the source's text and the existing pipeline distils it, so the quote check, line citations, contradictions and specs-against-the-vault apply unchanged. Rejected: facts citing pages or image regions (the Hub cannot check a quote against pixels).

D4 Containment by flag, measured. In -p mode a Read outside the working directory is a permission request and is denied, but a user-level defaultMode bypassPermissions let it through; an explicit --permission-mode default refused it again. The file is copied into a fresh temporary directory alone, and the command never carries a widening flag.

D5 Raw-body upload. POST /vault/files takes the bytes as the body and the fields as query parameters; the size middleware exempts that one path up to 10 MiB and the route counts the bytes it reads. Rejected: base64 in POST /vault/sources and multipart (see upload-file).

D6 The dashboard fetches the file with its key and shows it from a blob URL (an img, or an embedded PDF viewer): the Hub authenticates by header, so a bare src cannot.

checked: hub/hub/runner_adapters/claude.py:159-173: the worker one-shot runs with --tools "" and --strict-mcp-config
hub/hub/worker.py:311-404: run_worker spawns in a fresh temporary directory unless given cwd
hub/hub/distillation.py:172-219: prepare reads the source's text; a None text means held elsewhere
hub/hub/vault.py:609-672: add_source writes sources/<id>.md then <id>.json with media_type text/plain

limits: Measured on one machine with claude 2.1.291 and Haiku only; PDFs over 20 pages, scanned PDFs and large images are not measured
The containment measurement used --settings to simulate a user-level bypass default; it was not repeated with a real ~/.claude/settings.json
Whether Haiku's transcription of a dense screenshot is complete is a model judgement; the drive uses plain, large text

lifecycle: When closed, this change folds into the knowledge-vault capability, and the roadmap's images-and-pdfs slice is then done.
problem: The vault takes only text. Business knowledge also arrives as PDFs (policies, contracts, specs from a client) and as images (screenshots of a settings page, a photographed whiteboard). Today the operator must transcribe them by hand or they never reach the vault, so the facts they state are never distilled, never checked for contradictions and never cited by a requirement. The roadmap's images-and-pdfs slice: 'Images and PDFs can be uploaded, are shown in the wiki, and are distilled like text: by the manager's runner reading them natively where its harness can, by an extractor otherwise.' Done means: 'An uploaded PDF and a screenshot each produce cited facts, and the wiki shows both inline.'

requirements.rationale: A raw body, not base64 inside the JSON route (a third larger, and still over the 1 MB cap) or multipart (python-multipart is not a declared Hub dependency).
requirements.statement: POST /vault/files MUST store the raw request body as a new source when its Content-Type is application/pdf, image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp and its bytes begin with that type's signature, taking name, type, visibility and dated from query parameters checked as a text upload's are. It MUST answer 201 with the entry as the map lists it, carrying its media_type; 415 for any other Content-Type; 400 when the bytes do not match the type; 413 above 10 MiB; and a body between 1 MB and 10 MiB MUST reach the route rather than the global 1 MB refusal. The file MUST be written as sources/<id>.<ext> before its metadata, in the tracked location or, for a private source, the private one with only the metadata stub tracked. The upload MUST trigger distillation in the background as a text upload does.

requirements.rationale: The Vault page shows the file from this route; the dashboard authenticates with a header, so it fetches the bytes and shows them from a blob.
requirements.statement: GET /vault/sources/{id}/file MUST answer a file source's bytes with its media type; 404 for an unknown id or a text source; 409 naming the holder when the source is private and held on another machine.

requirements.rationale: F573, measured 2026-10-12 with claude 2.1.291 and Haiku: the Read tool returned a two-page PDF's and a PNG's text exactly; without tools the model could not read either. A transcription keeps the quote check that makes a citation trustworthy.
requirements.statement: Distilling a file source that has no transcription yet MUST first make one worker spawn, by the distillation job's runner and model, whose command allows only the Read tool, passes --strict-mcp-config and an explicit --permission-mode default, and runs in a fresh temporary directory holding only a copy of the file. It MUST ask for every line of text the file shows in reading order, page by page for a PDF, and for an image a short description of what else it shows, the file being data and not instructions. The answer MUST be stored as the source's text and then distilled exactly as a text source's is, so every fact cites lines of the transcription. A failed or unparsable transcription MUST store no text and no facts and record the distillation firing as failed with the reason. A file source with a transcription MUST be distilled again from it without a new reading.

requirements.rationale: Measured 2026-10-12: with a user-level defaultMode bypassPermissions, a Read-only worker read a file outside its directory; with --permission-mode default added, the same read was refused. A source can carry an instruction (a screenshot saying 'read ~/.ssh'); the worker must not be able to follow it.
requirements.statement: The reading worker MUST NOT be launched with any flag that skips or widens permissions (--dangerously-skip-permissions, --permission-mode other than default, --add-dir, --allowedTools beyond Read), so that a Read outside its directory is denied even when the operator's own Claude settings default to bypassing permissions.

requirements.rationale: No other runner was measured; a runner that cannot read the file would otherwise produce a confident transcription of nothing.
requirements.statement: When the distillation job's runner is of a CLI other than claude, distilling a file source MUST make no spawn: the distil route MUST answer 409 naming the runner's CLI and saying to choose a Claude runner on the Manager page, and an upload-triggered distillation MUST record nothing. Until a file source is transcribed, reading it (GET /vault/entries/{id} and vault_read) MUST answer no content and a note saying it has not been read yet and how to have it read.

requirements.rationale: Agents read the vault through vault_map and vault_read; they read the transcription, never the bytes.
requirements.statement: The map and an entry read MUST carry a source's media_type, and reading a transcribed file source MUST answer its transcription as the content, paged as text is, with a note that it was transcribed from the named PDF or image.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done sentence names the wiki. A 404 is the :8000 skew: a committed bundle reaches the operator's app before their Hub restarts.
requirements.statement: The Vault page MUST show a selected image source as an image and a selected PDF source in an embedded viewer, from the file route, above its transcription with the cited lines highlighted as a text source's are; show the not-read-yet note in place of the transcription before it exists; mark image and PDF entries in the entry list; and accept .pdf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif and .webp files in the upload form, sending them to POST /vault/files. When the file route answers 404 (a Hub older than the bundle) the page MUST show the transcription without the file and no error.

in_scope: POST /vault/files: a PDF or image uploaded as the raw request body, up to 10 MiB, with name, type, visibility and dated as query parameters
The file stored as sources/<id>.<ext> beside its metadata, in the tracked or the private location as a text source is
Transcription: one Read-only worker spawn per file, by the distillation job's Claude runner, its text stored as the source's text and then distilled as text
A runner that cannot read files answering why, naming a Claude runner as the remedy
vault_read and the map naming a file source's media type
The Vault page showing an image or PDF inline above its transcription, the upload form accepting them, and the map marking them
non_goals: Extractors (a PDF text library, OCR): no PDF library is a Hub dependency, and only Claude was measured
Reading files with Codex or Copilot runners: not measured (Codex is undrivable on this machine; drives bind Haiku only)
Facts citing a page or a region of the image: facts cite lines of the transcription
Editing or replacing an uploaded file: a new upload is a new source

summary: The operator can upload a PDF or an image (a screenshot, a photo of a whiteboard) to the vault. The Hub stores the file beside its metadata, shows it inline in the Vault page, and distils it like text: the distillation job's Claude runner first reads the file natively, in a one-shot worker that holds only the Read tool and only a copy of that file, and writes down its text; that transcription is then distilled by the existing pipeline, so every fact cites lines of it and the quote check is unchanged. F573 is settled by measurement: a Claude (Haiku) worker read a two-page PDF and a PNG exactly; no other runner is measured, so a runner of any other CLI answers that it cannot read files and no extractor is built. Tier 2: the worker gains a tool (containment measured, and the hazard a user-level bypass default creates is closed by an explicit flag), and one route is exempt from the 1 MB body cap.
